citation: DFARS 252.204-7012(c)(1)(ii) and (c)(2); definition of 'rapidly report' in 252.204-7012(a)
trigger: Discovery of a cyber incident that affects a covered contractor information system or the covered defense information in it (including the commercial suite once it held Supplier B drawings)
deadline: Within 72 hours of discovery. Report what is known; add updates as the review continues
notify: DoD at https://dibnet.dod.mil, using a DoD-approved medium assurance certificate (252.204-7012(c)(3)); report includes at least the elements listed on DIBNet
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - second-tier subcontractor with DFARS 252.204-7012 in Prime A and Supplier B purchase orders. President files; Office Manager is backup. No certificate yet (POAM-008)

obligation: Review for compromise of covered defense information
trigger: Same trigger as the DoD report
deadline: Starts at discovery; results feed the report and its updates
notify: Internal (results go to DoD in the report)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - identify compromised computers, accounts, and specific data, including other systems that may have been reached

obligation: Incident report number to the higher-tier contractor
trigger: After the DIBNet report is submitted and DoD assigns an incident report number
deadline: As soon as practicable
notify: Supplier B (next higher-tier subcontractor) and/or Prime A, whichever owns the affected CUI
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - flowed down in both customers' purchase orders

trigger: Malicious software discovered and isolated in connection with a reported incident
deadline: As instructed by DC3 or the Contracting Officer. Do not send malware to the Contracting Officer
notify: DoD Cyber Crime Center (DC3)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if malware is found (a mailbox takeover may leave none on company computers)

trigger: Discovery of a cyber incident
deadline: Keep for at least 90 days from submission of the report, so DoD can request the media or decline interest
notify: Internal custody (Office Manager); insurer panel forensics; MSP
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - images of known affected systems and relevant monitoring data (mailbox audit logs, message trace, sign-in logs)

obligation: DoD access for forensic analysis and damage assessment
trigger: DoD request for more information or equipment; Contracting Officer request for damage assessment information
deadline: On request
notify: DoD (through the Contracting Officer, via the higher-tier contractor)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - President is the point of contact

trigger: Incident involving CUI in the CUI suite (government-community cloud)
deadline: The provider must comply with paragraphs (c) to (g); coordinate so reports and preserved data are consistent
notify: CUI suite provider (support case and security contact from the CRM)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if SYS-01 is involved; not in the worked scenario unless analysis finds SYS-01 access

trigger: Empowered Official believes an ITAR violation may have occurred (for example, ITAR drawings forwarded to a foreign destination)
deadline: Voluntary. Initial notice immediately after the violation is discovered; full disclosure within 60 calendar days of the notice unless an extension is granted (127.12(c)(1))
notify: Directorate of Defense Trade Controls
applies_at_this_tier: Decision by the President (Empowered Official) with export counsel. Theft by an outside attacker may not be a company violation; document the reasoning either way

trigger: Company believes it may have violated the EAR (commercial parts with EAR-controlled technology)
deadline: Voluntary; a deliberate decision not to disclose a significant apparent violation is an aggravating factor (764.5(a))
notify: BIS Office of Export Enforcement
applies_at_this_tier: Decision by the President with export counsel

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (only if employee records in payroll, email, or the laptops are affected)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach (a 15-day extension for good cause applies to this notice only)
notify: Affected Florida residents (employees)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if personal information is involved. Not expected in this scenario (drawings, not personal data)

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company has 7 employees and holds no consumer data, so the 500-person threshold cannot be reached

obligation: Third-party agent notice to the company
trigger: A breach of security at the MSP or another third-party agent that maintains personal information for the company
deadline: Third-party agent must notify the company within 10 days of its determination
notify: The company (Office Manager), which then decides on notices
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the MSP or payroll service has a breach of company personal information; plus the 24-hour contract term planned in POAM-009

trigger: Personal information of residents of other states
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Residents and regulators per each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Only if personal information of non-Florida residents is involved (no current employees live outside Florida)

trigger: Customer C technical data affected
deadline: Per contract terms
notify: Customer C
applies_at_this_tier: Contractual, not legal. President checks the agreement

trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy (call the carrier's hotline before hiring vendors)
notify: Carrier breach hotline (President holds the policy)
applies_at_this_tier: Contractual, not legal

trigger: Security incident at the MSP or in its tools (RMM, backup) affecting the company
deadline: No term today; 24 hours once the amendment is signed (POAM-009, due 2026-10-31)
notify: Office Manager and President
applies_at_this_tier: Contractual, not legal

trigger: Suspected theft of controlled technical information by a criminal or foreign actor
deadline: As soon as practical
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Recommended; coordinate with the DIBNet report

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering any payment to an extortionist
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Only if extortion occurs. POL-03 4.8 requires President, counsel, and insurer approval

trigger: Cyber incident on a classified information system
deadline: Immediately
notify: DCSA (Cognizant Security Office)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company has no facility clearance or classified systems

trigger: Discovery of covered telecommunications equipment or services during contract performance
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; mitigation details within 10 business days
notify: Contracting Officer (DoD: https://dibnet.dod.mil)
applies_at_this_tier: No - not triggered by this incident type; applies only if such equipment is found

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reports (PROPOSED)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours; 24 hours after ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; not a current obligation
